text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency spike on /v1/stream (streaming) — multiple clients reporting stalled chunks and reconnects. Error rate for streaming sessions up to 0.4%. Paging carla_oncall.
carla_oncall: Ack. I'm on it. @alice_sre @ben_runtime can you triage streaming stack? customer-impact flagged by support.
alice_sre: Looking at traces now. p95 mostly fine, p99 tail up ~4s -> 12s over the last 6m. Correlates with increase in downstream write queue and lots of slow socket writes on runtime pods.
ben_runtime: I'm seeing a surge in socket_write_time on streaming-runtime-2/3. Also proxy (envoy) shows downstream retries/timeouts around the same window. Possible client backpressure + proxy buffering. Pulling proxy config.
ben_runtime: envoys show a lot of delayed flushes: downstream_idle_timeout was 15s, keepalive intervals at default. Some clients are using slow SSE reconnect loops which cause partial flush backlog.
carla_oncall: Is this causing 502s or just stalls? we need to assess customer impact to determine pager escalation.
alice_sre: Primarily stalls — connections hold open but no chunks delivered for many seconds then clients reconnect. A minority (~0.02%) see HTTP 502 when proxy gives up. Impact: conversation UIs freeze for a portion of customers, some timeouts on SDKs.
david_support: We have two paying customers reporting degraded UX (chat UI freeze). I can DM them. Which sessions are affected? Any identifying metadata?
ben_runtime: Affected sessions cluster on pod shard streaming-runtime-2 in us-west-2. Client IPs show long-lived connections and high RTT. I'll paste a sample tail of logs.
ben_runtime: ```
[2026-03-12T14:07:12Z] stream_id=abc123 write_bytes=512 write_delay_ms=4200 downstream=envoy-5 timeout=0
[2026-03-12T14:07:13Z] stream_id=def456 write_bytes=64 write_delay_ms=9800 downstream=envoy-6 timeout=1
[2026-03-12T14:07:14Z] stream_id=ghi789 write_bytes=256 write_delay_ms=12300 downstream=envoy-5 timeout=0
```
carla_oncall: OK runtime, netops — propose mitigations: (A) lower proxy downstream_idle_timeout and enable more aggressive flushes for SSE; (B) scale streaming pool by +2 to spread slow clients; (C) temporary route 10% of streaming traffic to fallback non-streaming polling endpoint to reduce tail pressure. Which can we do quickly?
frank_netops: I can push a small envoy config change to enable flush interval and reduce idle timeout in traffic layer for streaming route. Need ~2–3m to roll to us-west-2.
ben_runtime: Scaling streaming-runtime by +2 replica is a 1-click in k8s; I'll apply HPA override and spin up now. Also can flip runtime flag `streaming.flush_interval_ms=100` (default 1000) to force more frequent flushes; small risk of more packets but reduces stall windows.
alice_sre: Quick check: increasing flush frequency helps chunked SSE with slow clients (prevents TCP write coalescing/backpressure). Also confirm KV cache isn't thrashing — looks stable.
carla_oncall: Action plan: 1) frank pushes envoy flush/idle changes to us-west-2, 2) ben scales runtime + toggles flush_interval flag, 3) apply 10% traffic split to polling fallback via routing rule. David will inform affected customers that we are mitigating.
david_support: Noted. I'll send initial status to customers and add that we have a mitigation plan.
frank_netops: Rolling envoy change: updating route `streaming-route` set `downstream_idle_timeout=5s` and `stream_flush_interval=100ms`. Command:
```
kubectl apply -f envoy-streaming-patch.yaml --context=prod-us-west-2
```
frank_netops: Patch applied. Rolling restart of envoy pods started (svc/streaming-proxy). ETA ~90s per pod.
ben_runtime: Increasing runtime replicas: `kubectl scale deploy/streaming-runtime --replicas=6 -n prod` — done. Flipping flush flag via configmap update and forcing rollout.
ben_runtime: ```
kubectl set env deploy/streaming-runtime STREAMING_FLUSH_MS=100 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/streaming-runtime -n prod
```
carla_oncall: Routing change for 10% fallback: applying routing rule via runtime-router feature flag.
carla_oncall: ```
POST /admin/traffic-split
{ "route": "/v1/stream", "fallback": "/v1/poll", "percent": 10 }
```
carla_oncall: Rule applied. Monitoring metrics.
alice_sre: Metrics update: within 2 min, p99 dropped from ~12s to ~3.1s. Error reconnects decreased. streaming write_delay_ms median down 60% on affected pods.
ben_runtime: Logs show far fewer long write_delay entries. Envoy rollouts finished 3m ago.
frank_netops: Confirmed lowered downstream buffer usage and flushes happening faster.
david_support: Sent update to customers: "We deployed mitigations (proxy and runtime flushing, partial traffic fallback). You may see some reconnects but overall stability should improve." They replied :thumbsup: to the first customer.
carla_oncall: Good. I'll continue monitoring for 30m then hand off to night team. Any follow-ups for the postmortem?
emily_prod: Please capture exact trigger: why did backpressure start now? Check recent client SDK change? Also add a synthetic test for SSE chunk delivery under slow clients and set alert on sustained streaming write_delay_ms > 2s.
alice_sre: Agreed. We'll add regression alert and a circulating synthetic that simulates high-latency clients. Also will collect a set of traces for top 3 customers for root-cause.
ben_runtime: I'll file a runtime ticket to investigate flush heuristics and consider adaptive flush based on downstream RTT. Also check kernel TCP buffers / netem profiles for problematic ISPs.
carla_oncall: Handoff: I am handing off to alice_sre for the next 8h watch. Current state: mitigations applied, p99 improved, some residual reconnects but error rate within baseline. Follow-ups: postmortem, synthetic test, expand routing fallback to be dynamic if tail reappears.
alice_sre: Taking handoff. I will run through checklist and sync with eng-runtime tomorrow. tagging follow-ups: ENG-STREAM-674 (postmortem), ENG-STREAM-675 (synthetic), OPS-STREAM-88 (routing fallback automations).
carla_oncall: Thanks team. Closing the active pager. If anything spikes, page oncall again and use this thread as handoff record. :white_check_mark:
ben_runtime: noted, keeping logs/pss exported to /var/reports/streaming-2101234567.tar.gz for the postmortem.
frank_netops: I'll push a small runbook update for envoys to mention `stream_flush_interval` setting for streaming routes.
david_support: Customers acknowledged. I'll coordinate any follow-up support tickets.
emily_prod: We'll prioritize the synthetic in next sprint. Thanks everyone.
incident-bot: Incident status set to mitigated by carla_oncall at 2101234688. Pager closed."
